The *Ekadīpiyattheraapadāna* (Tha Ap 179) is a short biographical poem in the *Therāpadāna* section of the Pali Khuddaka Nikāya [SuttaCentral]. Like other texts in the collection, it preserves the narrative verse recounting the past meritorious deeds and karmic fruits of an individual elder (*thera*).

No direct external parallels in Chinese, Sanskrit, or Tibetan Buddhist corpora are identified by SuttaCentral or DharmaNexus [SuttaCentral; DharmaNexus]. However, automated analysis via DharmaNexus indicates Pali-internal text reuse with another Apadāna text: it shares two matching passages totaling 381 characters with the *Ekacāriyattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 191), with the most substantial alignment linking segments 3.1–6.1 of Tha-Ap 179 with segments 5.1–8.1 of Tha-Ap 191 [DharmaNexus].

No detailed discussions or citations of this text were identified in the indexed secondary reference literature. SuttaCentral records five modern translations of the text across five languages [SuttaCentral].
